Jim Heathfield was second, a position he usually occupies in Club championship races over this distance, and Alan Bishop was third. Peter Casselton retained his 440 junior title with J.
Jim Heathfield won the 440 senior with Alan Bishop second and J.

Alan Bishop was a good second in the 880 yds., which was won in 2 min. 1.5 secs., while Stan Davies and George Stace scored in the 1 mile. Our juniors won their 4 x 110 relay but the seniors were just beaten in a close finish in the closing darkness.
Ian Badiali won the 440 yds. in the good time of 51.5 secs., and Jack Brown was second to Terry Higgins in the 880 in 1 min. 57 secs., with Alan Bishop in third place

John Burr, 99th, Alan Bishop, 219th, and Len Bishop 247th, completed our team, and but for the backward position of the latter two, we should have stood a good chance of once again winning the “ Charles Otway ” Cup, which is awarded to the first club finishing its complete team, outside the three placed clubs.

Jack Brown won the 1½ miles in another new track record time of 6 mins. 58.2 secs., while in the 3 mile event we had Bob Belmore 4th and Don Maclean 5th. The medley relay saw Alan Bishop give us the lead over the half-mile stage, but Essex Beagles beat us into 2nd place in 3 mins. 54 secs.

Alan Bishop was our only runner in the 880 yards and could not gain a point but we did better in the mile which Cliff Roffey won in 4.24.8. Jim Masters won the two miles in 9m. 46.6s. but again he had no second string to support him.

The best feature of the race was the expected tussle between Jack Brown, John Burr and Cliff Roffey, and an exciting battle it was with the three of them coming home within 2 seconds of each other. It was good to see Alan Bishop picking up a pot.
A special word of praise for Alan Bishop. From a mediocre half miler (he won't mind me saying that) to 29th in the Poly Marathon in such a short space of time is no mean feat.
Eric and Alan Bishop who were fourth at the start, moved up to 2nd place having run an extremely well judged race. The positions of the other pairs changed very little throughout the event.

Eddie Short 28th, looked fairly happy and so did Eric and Alan Bishop who were now 32nd and 45th respectively. Between them was Brian Trower who shouted out that he was going to retire, but the reception given to his remark made him decide to finish the course.

Others to complete the course were Freddie Bradnum 53rd, Wally Wortley 61st and Alan Bishop 82. Ivor Edmonds started but was suffering from a rather badly swollen leg and decided to drop out at 9 miles.
Wortley and Freddie Bradnum both retired and Alan Bishop dropped back over the last 5 miles which lost him a standard medal.
It was good to see our London to Brighton men, Alan Bishop, MacDonald and Wortley sharpening up early in the season, it is hoped they will soon be starting their long preparation.
Unfortunately Eric is allergic to the sun and after about two miles he began to drop back and on Copse Hill he was overtaken by Alan Bishop, who then led in the Club Championship.

Other Club members taking part were, Eric Gebbett 23rd in 2H.42m.56s., Alan Bishop 29th in 2h.51m.7s. and Eric Bishop 36th in 3h.1m.57s. The latter did very well to finish the course as he had only one month's training in preparation for this race, having had achilles tendon trouble since the early part of the year.
Good performances came from Steve Charlton, J.Moore and Alan Bishop, whilst new-comer R.Bhatia from Ceylon, astounded most of us by running well to the front and finishing in 8th position.
Special mention must go to our first and last man; to Pat Newell on his excellent 14th place and Alan Bishop for his most creditable 151st on this very fast course.

Then came Len Bishop in 3rd. place Eric 9th, Bob Glover (coerced into running by Ken Stimpson) 10th!, with Alan Bishop, Joe Dooley and Bob Plummer running well together in 14th position - 1 min.49 secs. down on the leaders.

Don Maclean was having one of his days and was lying 120th and Alan Bishop completed our contingent in 125th place. Our first man home was Eric Bishop, with brothers Alan and Len in 109th and 125th positions. Eric was followed in by Jim Heathfield, who is finding it very difficult to do any serious training now that he has changed his job.

Marathon on July 8th was Alan Bishop who finished sixth in 2 : 51 : 05.

We also extend congratulation to Jill and Len Bishop on the birth of their daughter Angela. Eric Bishop won this particular race several years ago with his son Clive and it now only remains for brother Alan to close in for Bishop Harriers!

With three to score for the Jim Peters Trophy our boys beat the Bristol leading trio by 16 points, and in the Fry Trophy competition for six runners our first three boys together with D.W.Jones (55) Len (64) and Alan Bishop (67) beat Epsom & Ewell Harriers by one point after a recount.

Alan Bishop finished 15th in the S.L.H.'30' on August 31st, clocking a best ever 3:27:10.
Alan Bishop, one of the 'regulars' in this field, ran his usual steady, reliable race to complete the team and give us a one-point win from Wakefield H.

We could only field three runners, Charlie Walker 18th (83:37), John Moore 27th (84:50) and Alan Bishop 77th (92:00). Derby were the winners with 14 points and Belgrave 8th with 89 points.

In the Exeter to Plymouth 44 miles road race on May 9th,Alan Bishop(5:52:3) finished 4th and Wally Wortley(6:27:26) was 7th. Wally led at 5 miles but was overtaken by our own Norman Stairs who went way ahead to lead by 3½ minutes at'20'.

On the same day as the Southall'10',Norman Stairs and Alan Bishop ran in the SLH'30' at Coulsdon.Norman was 7th at the marathon distance in 2:51:20 but the oppresive conditions forced him to call it a day- Alan completed the "additional" 4 miles to finish 24th in 4:02:08.
Yet again Wally Wortley and Alan Bishop made up the Belgrave team,which was the second English club to close in. Norman Stairs breaks away in the London-Brighton Run.

Geoff Pearson, Alan Bishop and Len Bishop represented Belgrave in the second Oxfam Marathon, Alan completing his qualification for a Club second class standard.
